family.description: TTR-52 was called family 2 in [[cite:PUB00001984]], and has weak similarity to transthyretin (formerly called pre-albumin) which transports thyroid hormones. The specific function of this protein is as a bridging molecule in apoptosis cross-linking dying cells to phagocytes. TTR-52 bridges by cross-linking surface-exposed phosphatidylserine (PtdSer) on apoptotic cells to the CED-1 receptor, a transmembrane receptor, on phagocytes. TTR-52 has an open beta-barrel-like structure [[cite:PUB00109168]].
family.name: Transthyretin-like family

causal_graphs.context: 2010 Figure 1C; sm211 backcrossed four times to N2. Thirty-three corpses from three WT embryos and 32 from three mutant embryos were followed. Four-dimensional microscopy of 300-min embryos uses 118 mM NaCl/48 mM KCl egg buffer, 26-um stacks with 1.3-um spacing, every 5 min for 150 min. Displayed mean durations are 28 +/- 2 versus 55 +/- 6 min, SEM.

evidence.explanation: Figure 1C and author-PDF microscopy Methods support longer durations with the nested embryo/corpse sample counts explicitly preserved.
evidence.snippet: average duration almost twice as long

evidence.explanation: Reference mapping and the exact deposited cDNA translation link the tested gene to this family; neither proves isolated-domain sufficiency or verifies every experimental mutant sequence.

edges.mechanism: Corpses persist longer in the backcrossed mutant than in N2 under the same microscopy comparison, supporting impaired clearance. The observation does not resolve a direct domain-specific chemical mechanism or imply more cells initiate apoptosis.
edges.subject: sm211-v43m-versus-n2

causal_graphs.family_mapping: G5ED35 ttr-52/F11F1.7 has 135 residues, sequence version 1, exact UniProt/InterPro agreement and PF01060 at 28-112 inclusive. The study's deposited HM130527.1 translation ADO60153.1 matches G5ED35 exactly. V43 lies inside the match; sm211 is V43M, not the distinct tm2078 deletion.
causal_graphs.limitations: Corpses are nested within six embryos, not 65 independent embryo replicates. Exact imaging temperature and handling of the >110-min histogram bin remain unresolved. Gene mapping and corpse-count rescue support the target but do not separately rescue every lifetime endpoint. Altered localization can mediate V43M effects; no unique ligand-contact chemistry or increased apoptosis is inferred.

nodes.label: Duration of visible embryonic cell corpses

causal_graphs.scope: Whole-animal C. elegans ttr-52(sm211) phenotype compared with N2 Bristol, not an isolated-domain biochemical reaction or a gene-null allele.
causal_graphs.title: The sm211 V43M allele increases embryonic corpse persistence

causal_graphs.context: Pced-1CED-1::GFP marks corpses identified by Nomarski morphology. Serial optical sections span 20 um at 1-um spacing. Fifteen embryos per stage and genotype, SEM; the adopted 1.5-fold comparison is approximately 64% versus 34% labeled corpses with reported P < 0.0001. Comma-stage data are a separate comparison.

evidence.explanation: Figure 4B and the corresponding Results support the decreased labeled fraction; the exact stage and reporter background constrain this edge.

edges.mechanism: The mutant background has fewer ring-positive corpses at the matched embryonic stage. This supports a TTR-52-dependent effect on receptor localization without identifying a direct V43 contact or proving the full engulfment trajectory.
edges.subject: sm211-in-ced1-gfp-background

causal_graphs.family_mapping: sm211 changes V43 to M in G5ED35, within PF01060 28-112. Reference sequence version 1 matches the study's HM130527.1 protein translation exactly. Intact secreted TTR-52 is the implicated protein, not a purified 28-112 fragment.
causal_graphs.limitations: Reporter rings are a cellular localization endpoint, not a molecular binding constant or a directly tracked recruitment-to-engulfment chain. V43M can change secretion/localization and is not interchangeable with a deletion. Separate pull-down and co-IP experiments show association, not automatic receptor activation. No endpoint-specific rescue or raw image reanalysis is claimed here.

causal_graphs.scope: CED-1::GFP localization in 1.5-fold C. elegans embryos carrying smIs34, compared with smIs34;ttr-52(sm211), in the 2010 Figure 4B experiment.
causal_graphs.title: The sm211 allele decreases CED-1 ring labeling around corpses

causal_graphs.context: With versus without transgene expression, scored in 1.5-fold embryos after 1 h heat shock at 33 C and recovery at 20 C, examined 3.5 h after treatment. Two independent transgenic lines, n >= 15 per line, SEM. The graph adopts the WT rescue comparison, not all substitution or truncation constructs in the same figure.

evidence.explanation: Figure 3 upper-panel WT bars and heat-shock Methods support the decrease; two lines and at least 15 embryos per line are reported. No precise count was digitized for this graph.

edges.mechanism: The induced WT transgene condition has fewer persistent corpses than the condition without transgene expression. This genetic rescue is kept separate from sm211 and the purified lipid-binding assay rather than joined into a directly observed molecular sequence.
edges.subject: heat-shock-wt-ttr52-expression

causal_graphs.family_mapping: Full-length G5ED35 sequence version 1 contains PF01060 at 28-112 and agrees with the 2010 deposited cDNA translation. The signal region 1-20 and C-terminal I113/L132 are outside the current profile. Complete transgene junctions and tm2078 deletion boundaries remain unverified.
causal_graphs.limitations: Corpse count supports genetic rescue of a clearance phenotype, not direct measurement of single-corpse duration or prevention of apoptosis. The comparison follows a heat-shock expression protocol; it does not establish an isolated protein-dose effect independent of that intervention. Variant-label discrepancies elsewhere in Figure 3 are excluded from this WT edge.

Persistent cell corpse count in 1.5-fold tm2078 embryos

causal_graphs.scope: Full-length WT TTR-52::mCherry under heat-shock promoters in the ttr-52(tm2078) deletion background, 2012 Figure 3 upper panel. This is not the sm211 allele or its lifetime assay.
causal_graphs.title: WT TTR-52 transgene expression reduces persistent corpse counts in tm2078

causal_graphs.context: P-6001 lipid strips; 25 mM Tris-HCl pH 7, 150 mM NaCl, 0.1% Tween 20, 0.1 mM ZnSO4 and 0.2 mM CaCl2. Block 1 h at 22 C with 1% dried milk; protein incubation overnight at 4 C without milk, three washes, anti-Flag detection. Anti-TTR-52 blot checks protein presence. Two independent experiments; exact protein dose is not specified.

evidence.explanation: Figure 4 D51A strip compared with the WT TBS/cation strip, accompanied by the protein blot, supports reduced binding rather than an affinity constant or observed metal geometry.

edges.mechanism: D51A yields less PtdSer-spot signal than WT under the stated strip conditions. The effect does not uniquely establish a direct D51-lipid or D51-metal contact and can include folding differences.
edges.subject: d51a-strip-preparation

evidence.explanation: Figure 4 D80A and WT cation-containing strips support the direction. Other lipid signals and the lack of exact protein-dose normalization constrain interpretation.

edges.mechanism: D80A yields less PtdSer-spot signal than WT, with protein detected by immunoblot. The result supports a substitution effect on this binding endpoint, not unique ion coordination or complete loss of all lipid association.
edges.subject: d80a-strip-preparation

evidence.explanation: Figure 4 N85A strip and WT cation-containing comparator support reduced PtdSer signal. The graph does not join this endpoint to separate worm phenotypes as an observed causal chain.

edges.mechanism: N85A decreases PtdSer-spot signal relative to WT in the same stated protocol. This does not directly show the proposed N85 geometry, an intact bilayer interaction or a downstream engulfment event.
edges.subject: n85a-strip-preparation

causal_graphs.family_mapping: D51, D80 and N85 match G5ED35 sequence version 1 and lie within PF01060 at 28-112. The study's earlier cDNA deposit matches this reference exactly. Full-length secreted fusion preparations are not isolated domain fragments; cleavage and fusion junctions remain construct-specific uncertainties.
causal_graphs.limitations: Directness concerns the measured immobilized-lipid binding endpoint, not atomic ion coordination, bilayer insertion or receptor activation. Blot presence is not exact equimolar loading or a folding control. Other lipid signals remain visible in mutant strips. The crystallized six-alanine M5 protein and modeled WT coordinates do not directly show a WT binding trajectory. The 2010 strip protocol has tenfold higher cation concentrations and is not merged here.

evidence.explanation: Main Results, selected figures and author-PDF Methods support the sm211 contexts and link the deposited sequence. All supplementary figures, movies and raw microscopy were not reviewed.

Figures 3/4 and relevant Methods support tm2078 WT rescue and three lipid-strip substitutions. The text uses I113R/L132K whereas Figure 3 labels I113R/L132R; M5 labeling descriptions also conflict. These constructs are excluded from adopted substitution edges.

discussions.notes: Resolve tm2078 boundaries, clone/fusion sequences, exact protein dose, folding controls, imaging temperature, censoring and M5/double-mutant discrepancies. discussions.prompt: Resolve TTR-52 construct discrepancies and extend the receptor and lipid mechanism with separately scoped evidence.
discussions.rationale: Cellular clearance, CED-1 labeling and in-vitro lipid-strip effects are different endpoints. Source inconsistencies concern M5 corpse labeling and the C-terminal double mutant; they cannot be silently combined into a complete observed engulfment mechanism.
